title: Amazon launches first internet satellites since Vulcan Centaur failure
content:
Amazon is set to launch a new batch of its internet satellites on Monday, November 23. An Ariane 6 rocket will carry 36 Amazon Leo satellites from the European Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana. The launch window opens at 6:09 a.m. Eastern Standard Time (1109 GMT; 8:09 a.m. local time in Kourou) and is scheduled to last 29 minutes. Viewers can watch the event live on Space.com, with coverage beginning about 30 minutes before lift‑off.

The Amazon Leo constellation is designed to operate in low‑Earth orbit and will compete with SpaceX’s Starlink network, which currently has more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon plans a total of over 3,200 satellites for its network; to date, roughly 400 have reached orbit. The November 15 launch that was intended to deliver 40 additional satellites failed when a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur rocket suffered a problem shortly after liftoff, causing the loss of those spacecraft.

Amazon has booked additional rides on other launch vehicles, including ULA’s Atlas V, Blue Origin’s New Glenn, and SpaceX’s Falcon 9. The Vulcan Centaur will remain grounded while ULA investigates the failure. New Glenn has not flown since April, when it failed to place AST SpaceMobile’s BlueBird 7 satellite into the correct orbit, and it exploded during a pre‑launch test on May 28.

The Ariane 6, which debuted in July 2024, has completed nine launches, all successful except its maiden mission, which was a partial failure. The November 23 flight will be the fourth Amazon Leo mission launched by Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.
summary: An Ariane 6 rocket launched 36 Amazon Leo satellites from Kourou, French Guiana, eight days after a Vulcan Centaur failure destroyed 40 spacecraft. This mission marks the fourth Amazon Leo flight for Ariane 6 and the first since the November 15 launch anomaly.
author: Space.com

title: Max Verstappen wins Las Vegas F1 GP after final-lap Ferrari collision
content:
Max Verstappen secured a dramatic victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix after a race characterized by intense competition and on-track incidents. The Dutch Red Bull driver led the final lap to claim the win, capping off a contest in which the lead changed hands 34 times. Despite being under siege throughout the event, Verstappen maintained his position to finish ahead of his rivals.

The race featured a collision between Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton, adding to the spectacle of the event. The article describes the competition as an old-school duel involving slipstreaming, noting that it provided a significant display for the sport. Verstappen’s performance is highlighted as evidence of his status among Formula One’s greats, with the unique nature of the race attributed to the specific conditions of this season.
summary: Max Verstappen secured victory in the Las Vegas Grand Prix after Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton collided on the final lap. The race featured 34 lead changes, with the Red Bull driver maintaining the lead throughout the decisive final lap.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mets Seal $450M, 9-Year Deal with Pitcher Tarik Skubal
content: The New York Mets have reportedly signed free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal to a nine-year contract worth $450 million, marking the largest deal for a pitcher in Major League Baseball history. According to a report by Jon Heyman of The New York Post, this agreement surpasses the previous record held by Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who signed a 12-year, $325 million deal with the Dodgers in 2024. The move represents the biggest transaction of MLB’s current offseason for the Mets, a team that has missed the playoffs for the last two seasons.
summary: The New York Mets signed free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal to a $450 million, nine‑year contract, the largest pitcher deal in MLB history. The previous record was a $325 million, 12‑year contract for Yoshinobu Yamamoto with the Dodgers in 2024.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pochettino’s New Manager Bounce Falls Flat After De Ligt Move
content:
Manchester United’s decision to pick a Dutch defender over Harry Maguire backfired when the team collapsed in the Anfield bearpit, losing 4‑0 to Liverpool, United’s fiercest rivals.  

The defeat marked the poorest opening result of the eight managers who have followed Sir Alex Ferguson since May 2013. Under new head coach Mauricio Pochettino, the loss has left the manager in despair.
summary: Manchester United fell apart in a 4-0 loss to Liverpool at Anfield after choosing the Dutch defender over Harry Maguire. The defeat, the worst opening result of the eight managers since Sir Alex Ferguson, left Mauricio Pochettino in despair.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Bills defeat Dolphins, Bears maintain strong start, Ravens suffer sixth loss
content:
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen was limited to a four-yard touchdown pass and two interceptions in a win over the Miami Dolphins, while the team’s defense secured the victory against the injury-depleted rivals. James Cook contributed a one-yard rushing touchdown and 89 yards on the ground, becoming the NFL’s second player to score a touchdown and top 75 rushing yards in nine consecutive games. The Bills improved to a 9-1 record, while Miami fell to 1-9 after losing four straight games, marking their worst start to a season since opening 2007 with a 0-13 record.

In other NFL results, the Kansas City Chiefs and Detroit Lions continued their strong starts, while the Baltimore Ravens suffered their sixth consecutive loss. The Chicago Bears also maintained their strong start to the season. Additionally, Michael Metcalf was ejected for an eye poke during a loss for the Pittsburgh Steelers, as noted in the roundup’s headline.
summary: Bills defeat Dolphins, Bears maintain strong start, Ravens suffer sixth loss.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Alcaraz defeats Zverev 6‑2, 7‑6 to win first ATP Finals title
content:
Carlos Alcaraz captured his first ATP Finals title after defeating Alexander Zverev 6‑2, 7‑6 (7) in the final.  The Spaniard, who is the new world No 1, became the fourth player to win both a career Grand Slam and the ATP Finals.

The match underscored that the ATP world No 1 ranking and the title of the best male tennis player are held by different players.  This distinction had been apparent throughout the season, but it was highlighted again in the grand finale.

Alcaraz’s season had been hampered by a wrist injury that kept him out for four and a half months during the spring and summer.  Despite that setback, he completed the two most important objectives on his to‑do list for the year.
summary: Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz beat Alexander Zverev 6‑2, 7‑6 (7) to win his first ATP Finals title. The match confirmed Alcaraz as the new world No 1 while the titles of ATP world No 1 and best male player remain separate.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pochettino slams Yoro red card as Man United suffer 4-0 debut loss to Liverpool
content:
Manchester United lost 4‑0 to Liverpool at Anfield, marking the club’s joint‑heaviest debut defeat. Mauricio Pochettino said Leny Yoro was wrongly sent off early and that Manchester United were denied a penalty earlier in the match.

The 4‑0 result matched Lal Hilditch’s 1926 record of losing a first United game by that scoreline. Manchester United have conceded 34 goals across all competitions this season, the most by any team in Europe’s top five leagues.
summary: Manchester United were beaten 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield, matching the joint‑heaviest debut defeat in the club’s history. Manager Mauricio Pochettino said Leny Yoro’s red card was wrong and that United had been denied a penalty earlier in the match.
author: Guardian Sport

content: Manchester United are reportedly eyeing Al‑Ahli striker Ivan Toney. Fulham are holding contract talks with Calvin Bassey, while Paris Saint‑Germain may step up their pursuit of Eli Junior Kroupi.

content: Gerwyn Price secured his first major PDC title in four years by defeating Gian van Veen in the Grand Slam of Darts final. Price won the match with a score of 16-11, ending his long wait for a major championship victory.
summary: Gerwyn Price defeated Gian van Veen 16-11 in the Grand Slam of Darts final. The victory ended his four-year wait for a major PDC title.

content: Match of the Day pundit Danny Murphy highlighted Rio Ngumoha’s performance in Liverpool’s 4-0 victory over Manchester United. Murphy explained that Ngumoha demonstrated his capabilities, describing him as a game-changer for the team.
summary: Danny Murphy, a Match of the Day pundit, praised Rio Ngumoha for his performance. Ngumoha helped Liverpool secure a 4-0 victory over Manchester United.

content: The Democratic National Committee has announced recent layoffs in its digital operations, affecting many staff who contributed to the party’s recent electoral success. Critics argue that the DNC must maintain permanent infrastructure to preserve the momentum it has built as it prepares for the 2028 election.
summary: The Democratic National Committee recently laid off many employees in its digital operations. Critics argue the committee must maintain permanent infrastructure to sustain momentum toward the 2028 election.

content: A growing number of U.S. ports are reporting a surge of cyberattacks, many of which are AI‑enabled and target key infrastructure. The Port of Corpus Christi, Texas, the nation’s largest oil export passage, stated it was hit with “hundreds if not thousands” of attacks daily.

content: Democrats have secured the largest House majority in a regular election in decades, buoyed by significant 2026 midterm gains in historically challenging regions. Decision Desk HQ projects the party will hold 258 seats in the next Congress.
summary: Democrats have secured the largest House majority in a regular election in decades, following their 2026 midterm victories in historically challenging regions. Decision Desk HQ projects the party will hold 258 seats in the next Congress.

content:
Jeffries is set to lead the largest Democratic caucus since the 1990s, facing growing pains from policy disagreements and sprawling investigations.  

Democrats celebrated after exceeding midterm expectations, picking up almost 50 new House seats.
summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N. Y.) is set to take over the largest Democratic Caucus since the 1990s, and with it, potential headaches stemming from policy disagreements and sprawling investigations.

title: Lawmakers pause for Thanksgiving as year‑end agenda approaches
content:
Lawmakers are home for Thanksgiving, but the holiday break will be brief as they prepare to return to a packed legislative agenda.  

With Democrats slated to take control of both chambers in January, Republicans have only a few weeks left to advance their priorities before the clock on their power expires.
summary: Lawmakers are home for Thanksgiving but will have little time to enjoy the break before returning to a packed legislative agenda. Democrats are set to take control of both chambers in January, leaving Republicans only a few weeks to push through their priorities before their power expires.

title: Russian ship in Benghazi hit by suspected Ukrainian drone attack
content: Libyan officials reported that the Russian navy corvette Merkury, docked at a naval base in Benghazi, sustained severe damage during a suspected Ukrainian drone attack on Sunday. The vessel was struck by two sea drones, which triggered an explosion and a fire. An initial investigation into the incident is currently underway.
summary: The Russian navy corvette Merkury docked at a Benghazi naval base was struck by two sea drones, causing an explosion and fire. Libyan officials say the attack is suspected to be Ukrainian.
author: The Hill

title: Mayor Mamdani releases 84,000 additional 9/11 records
content:
Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) released an additional 84,000 records related to the September 11, 2001 attacks.  
The release follows a prior disclosure that revealed city leaders had lied about air quality. Mamdani said that after the terror attacks and the resulting health consequences, New Yorkers across the five boroughs demanded transparency.
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) released 84,000 additional records related to the September 11, 2001 attacks. The release followed a prior one that revealed city leaders had lied about air quality.
author: The Hill

title: Most governments reject meaningless agreement at Cop31 in Antalya
content:
The recent failure of COP31 in Antalya marked a “line in the sand” moment, according to Bill Hare. Nations stood together against major fossil‑fuel producers and rejected the draft text, a move Hare describes as a victory for multiculturalism. The agreement they turned down barely acknowledged the catastrophic climate emergency facing the world, nor did it signal a decisive shift away from fossil fuels.

Hare notes that the “good news” is that most governments rejected an agreement “stripped of meaning.” He also highlights the need for scrutiny of the influence wielded by Saudi Arabia, a key fossil‑fuel producer, in the negotiations.

Finally, Hare points out that co‑chairing global climate talks is not something that should be repeated, especially not by Australia. He concludes that the experiment “didn’t work.”
summary: Most governments at Cop31 in Antalya rejected an agreement stripped of meaning. Australia will not co‑chair future global climate talks, and Saudi Arabia's influence is under scrutiny.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Cannabidiol ineffective for behavioral problems in children with intellectual disability
content: A world‑first randomized controlled trial has determined that cannabidiol (commonly referred to as CBD) is not effective for treating severe behavioral problems in children with intellectual disability.
summary: A world-first randomized controlled trial found that cannabidiol is not effective in treating severe behavioral problems in children with intellectual disability. The study concluded that CBD does not help with these issues.

title: Cellas Hayes investigates blood vessel damage's link to memory loss
content: A new study by Cellas Hayes, Ph. D., of the University of Kentucky investigates how damage to brain blood vessels may contribute to memory loss. The research suggests that vascular changes can play a role in cognitive decline, offering a perspective beyond the usual focus on Alzheimer’s disease.
summary: Alzheimer's disease is often the focus when someone develops memory problems. But changes in the brain's blood vessels may also be part of the picture—and new research by the University of Kentucky's Cellas Hayes, Ph.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Expert Mateusz Łabuz warns AI erodes trust and ability to discern reality
content: Mateusz Łabuz warns in his new book, The End of Reality, that generative AI poses a danger beyond technical glitches. According to Łabuz, it gradually erodes our ability to discern what is real, undermines trust in institutions, and hampers independent thinking.
summary: Mateusz Łabuz says generative AI is causing a slow erosion of people's ability to tell what is real, trust institutions, and think for themselves. He presents these warnings in his new book, The End of Reality.

title: Common drugs may cause lasting gut microbiome changes, study finds
content: A study of more than 2,500 people found that medications taken years or even long ago can produce lasting changes in the gut microbiome. Researchers identified microbial “fingerprints” from common drugs such as antidepressants, blood pressure medications, and anxiety treatments, persisting after cessation. Some anxiety medications produced effects comparable to broad‑spectrum antibiotics.
summary: A study of more than 2,500 people found that medications taken years ago can leave lasting changes in the gut microbiome. Researchers reported that common drugs including antidepressants, blood pressure medications and anxiety treatments leave microbial fingerprints, with some anxiety medications showing effects comparable to broad‑spectrum antibiotics.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Identify Gene That Helps Brain Immune Cells Contain Alzheimer Plaques
content: Scientists have identified a gene that enables brain immune cells to contain harmful plaques associated with Alzheimer’s. In mouse studies, malfunction of this gene accelerated toxic buildup and caused cognitive decline, suggesting that restoring its function could protect the brain.
summary: Scientists have identified a gene that helps brain immune cells contain harmful plaques linked to Alzheimer’s. In mice, when the gene malfunctioned, toxic buildup accelerated and cognitive abilities declined, suggesting that restoring its function could protect the brain.
author: Science Daily

title: Brown University discovers relativity alters heavy atom triple bonds
content:
Brown University researchers have reported a surprising discovery that challenges a long‑standing textbook explanation in chemistry. The study provides direct evidence that Einstein’s theory of relativity alters the way heavy atoms form triple bonds.

According to the researchers, relativistic effects cause normally distinct types of chemical bonds to blend together. This finding confirms a prediction that has been circulating for decades and suggests that the traditional rules of chemistry do not fully apply to heavy elements such as bismuth.
summary: Researchers at Brown University found direct evidence that Einstein's theory of relativity changes how heavy atoms form triple bonds, causing normally distinct types of chemical bonds to blend together. The discovery confirms a decades-old prediction and suggests that traditional chemistry rules do not fully apply to heavy elements such as bismuth.
author: Science Daily

title: AI tool finds bladder cancer warning signs up to five years early, detects 85% of cases
content:
Scientists have created an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85 % of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients.  

By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.
summary: The AI tool can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a study of nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns missed by conventional screening, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and reduce unnecessary invasive procedures.
author: Science Daily

title: Type 2 diabetes linked to 53% higher risk of Alzheimer’s, review of 40 studies finds
content: A major new review of 40 studies reports that individuals with type 2 diabetes have a 53 % higher risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease. The analysis estimates that nearly five out of every 1,000 people with type 2 diabetes develop Alzheimer’s each year. By concentrating on the relationship between these two conditions, the review aims to clarify a potentially serious link between metabolic health and brain health.
summary: A major new review of 40 studies found that people with type 2 diabetes have a 53% higher risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease. Researchers estimate that nearly five out of every 1,000 people with type 2 diabetes develop Alzheimer’s each year.
author: Science Daily

title: Study finds gap suggests black holes form from stars that skip supernova
content: Massive stars may be collapsing directly into black holes without generating the supernova explosions that astronomers normally anticipate. Researchers identified a surprising pattern in 257 observed black‑hole mergers, and they propose that these silent stellar disappearances could account for a substantial portion of the black‑hole population in the universe.
summary: Massive stars may quietly collapse into black holes without producing supernova explosions. A pattern in 257 black‑hole mergers suggests these silent stellar disappearances could explain a large population of black holes throughout the universe.
author: Science Daily

title: DNA component may have shielded early life from intense UV radiation
content: Scientists discovered that a component of DNA acts like a sunscreen, converting ultraviolet damage into forms that are easier to repair, which may explain how early life survived intense UV radiation on early Earth. The finding could help solve a decades‑old evolutionary mystery about life’s endurance under those harsh conditions.
summary: Scientists found that a key component of DNA can turn potentially destructive ultraviolet damage into a form that is easier to repair. The discovery may help solve a decades‑old evolutionary mystery about how life endured the harsh conditions of early Earth.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find 287 DNA variants linked to longevity in 194-year-old tortoise Jonathan
content: Jonathan, a 194‑year‑old giant tortoise, is the world’s oldest living land animal. Scientists studying his DNA have identified 287 distinct genetic variants that are associated with DNA‑repair mechanisms, inflammation control, insulin regulation and cancer suppression, offering a potential explanation for his exceptional longevity.
summary: Jonathan, a 194‑year‑old giant tortoise, is the world’s oldest living land animal. Researchers identified 287 unique genetic variants in his DNA that are associated with DNA repair, inflammation control, insulin regulation and cancer suppression.
author: Science Daily

title: Most England ICBs cut GP funding for NHS weight‑loss drug Mounjaro
content:
Patients in England may miss out on NHS weight‑loss injections after most integrated care boards (ICBs) withdrew funding for GP services. An inquiry by the GP magazine Pulse found that the drug, Mounjaro (tirzepatide), is no longer covered by many local services.

The investigation revealed that 21 of 36 ICBs have scrapped payments to practices for prescribing and monitoring the medication. Nine ICBs never offered a local enhanced service, and only four still retain one.

The findings highlight a growing gap in access to the potentially life‑changing treatment for eligible patients.
summary: An inquiry by GP magazine Pulse found that 21 of 36 integrated care boards in England have scrapped payments to practices for prescribing and monitoring Mounjaro, also known as tirzepatide. Nine ICBs never had a local enhanced service and only four still retain one, leaving many eligible patients at risk of missing NHS weight‑loss injections.
author: Guardian Science

title: Recent FAA, Outlook, and JPMorgan Chase outages signal more tech failures ahead
content:
Recent disruptions have highlighted the fragility of critical infrastructure. A nationwide FAA ground stop halted air traffic, a multi‑day Microsoft Outlook outage brought entire companies to a standstill, and a banking outage at JPMorgan Chase stopped transactions across the institution. These incidents underscore the growing frequency of major tech failures.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN that the American public must be ready for significant investment in upgrading systems and cybersecurity. He warned that any step change in technology—whether in compute or applications—will inevitably produce “bumps in the road.”

Microsoft President Brad Smith issued a statement in response to the outages, though the content of that statement was not detailed in the report.
summary: Over the past week, the United States experienced a nationwide FAA ground stop, a multi‑day Outlook outage that halted companies, and a banking outage at JPMorgan Chase. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN that further investment in system upgrades and cybersecurity will be needed as more technology disruptions are expected.
author: The Verge

title: Democrats win biggest US House majority in over three decades
content: Democrats have secured their largest majority in the U.S. House of Representatives in more than three decades. The result is described as a crushing blow to President Donald Trump and is expected to usher in two years of divided government, political confrontation and ambitious legislative battles.
summary: Democrats have secured their largest US House of Representatives majority in more than three decades. The outcome is described as a crushing blow to President Donald Trump and sets the stage for two years of divided government and ambitious legislative battles.

title: Morocco's Ramakech sculpture park features upside-down house and giant installations
content: Ramakech, an 11‑hectare sculpture park near Marrakech, showcases an upside‑down house, oversized furniture and figures with vegetable heads. French artist Jean‑François Fourtou created the installations, describing them as larger‑than‑life works that evoke childhood memories. The park’s surreal pieces invite visitors to experience a world turned upside down.
summary: The Ramakech sculpture park near Marrakech spans 11 hectares and includes an upside-down house, giant furniture and vegetable-headed figures. French artist Jean-François Fourtou created the larger-than-life installations to evoke childhood memories.
author: Euronews

title: Drone strikes damage homes and UN building in Khartoum, army blames Ethiopia
content: Drone strikes early Sunday damaged residential homes and a United Nations building in Khartoum, Sudan’s capital. The Sudanese army blamed neighboring Ethiopia for carrying out the attacks, noting that drone warfare has intensified as the country’s four‑year‑old conflict continues.
summary: Drone strikes damaged residential homes and a United Nations building in Khartoum early Sunday. The army accused neighbouring Ethiopia of launching the attacks as drone warfare intensifies in the country's four‑year conflict.

content: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot condemned arson attacks by settlers on Palestinian villages in the West Bank on Sunday, calling the acts “Jewish terrorism.” Israeli police opened an investigation into the attacks, which occurred nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority.

title: EU states reject 11th‑hour deal, causing collapse of COP31 talks in Turkey
content: EU member states objected Sunday to adopting an 11th-hour deal at the COP31 climate talks in Turkey because it omitted explicit references to fossil fuels, according to the bloc's presidency. This issue remains a major point of contention at the summit, which is occurring amid soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions fueled by the war in Iran.

title: Le Pen denies receiving confidential info from suspected civil servant
content: Marine Le Pen denied that she received confidential information from a civil servant suspected of leaking details of investigations to her National Rally (RN) party. She said she could not confirm whether other party members had benefited from the alleged leaks.
summary: French far‑right leader Marine Le Pen denied receiving confidential information from a civil servant suspected of leaking details of investigations to her National Rally (RN) party. She said she could not say whether others in the party had benefited.

title: Trump holds third meme‑coin gala in Virginia as Democrats claim conflict of interest
content:
Donald Trump is set to headline his third cryptocurrency gala on Sunday night at the Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia. The dinner will reward top holders of Trump’s meme coin, amid ongoing accusations from Democrats that the president is improperly profiting from his crypto ventures.

According to the event’s website, the dinner will feature meet‑and‑greets with Trump supporters, including boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, Shark Tank investor Kevin O’Leary, NBA champion Tristan Thompson, and mentalist Lior Suchard. The event is positioned as a celebration of the president’s cryptocurrency interests while critics continue to question the ethical implications of his involvement.
summary: Trump holds third meme‑coin gala in Virginia as Democrats claim conflict of interest.
author: Guardian World

title: US Army seeks emergency order to detonate bomb chemicals in Iowa despite safety concerns
content:
The U.S. Army plans to invoke emergency provisions in Iowa to avoid a court order that had paused the detonation of several tons of bomb‑making chemicals, saying that continued delays will increase danger as the weather turns colder.  

In a filing late Saturday, government lawyers told the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals that swift action is needed to protect Army personnel and surrounding communities, adding that protection of human health and the environment demands action now, not delay.
summary: US Army seeks emergency order to detonate bomb chemicals in Iowa despite safety concerns.
author: Guardian World

title: UK taxpayers hold over £1tn in offshore tax havens, HMRC data shows
content:
UK taxpayers now hold more than £1 trillion in offshore tax‑haven accounts, a figure that has crossed the £1 trillion threshold for the first time, according to HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) data. The data, obtained by the TaxWatch thinktank through freedom‑of‑information requests, shows a 10 % rise in the total value of balances held in financial centres such as Jersey and Panama between 2022 and 2024.

The increase has sparked concerns about the potential impact on the public purse, as higher offshore holdings could translate into lost tax revenue for the United Kingdom. The figures represent the latest available data on UK taxpayers’ offshore balances.
summary: UK taxpayers hold more than £1tn in offshore accounts, according to HMRC data obtained by TaxWatch. The offshore balances rose 10% between 2022 and 2024, raising concerns about potential losses to the public purse.
author: Guardian World

title: US intelligence chief Jay Clayton says he trusts Trump’s “friend” label for Putin
content:
U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on Sunday that he trusts President Donald Trump “completely” after Trump called Russian President Vladimir Putin “a friend” during their recent meeting in China. Clayton was pressed about the comment in media appearances that followed the trilateral summit with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Trump drew criticism at home and abroad, and on Saturday posted a photo of himself shaking hands with Putin captioned “My Friend.” Clayton noted the president’s warm description despite Putin being described as a chief U.S. adversary.
summary: US director of national intelligence Jay Clayton said he trusts President Donald Trump “completely” after Trump called Russian President Vladimir Putin “a friend” during their recent meeting in China. Trump later posted a photo of himself shaking hands with Putin with the caption “My Friend” following backlash.
author: Guardian World

title: Chris Bowen faces criticism after UN climate talks speech in Turkey
content:
Australian climate change minister Chris Bowen faces significant criticism for his role in the COP31 negotiations, where disagreements over fossil fuels created an unbridgeable gap between petrostates and climate reality. Although the failure is not solely his, the issue of naming fossil fuels as the primary driver of global heating remained a central point of contention.

Following a major speech at the UN climate talks in Turkey, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese dismissed claims that he failed to address this core problem. He noted that the speech was brief and that numerous elements were omitted, defending his approach to the discussion.
summary: Australia's climate change minister Chris Bowen will face a torrent of criticism after delivering a major speech to the UN climate talks in Turkey. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese dismissed criticisms that he had not named burning fossil fuels as the main cause of catastrophic global heating, saying the short speech could omit many points.
author: Guardian World

title: Molly Meldrum, Australian music broadcaster and Countdown host, dies at 83
content:
Molly Meldrum, the longtime host of the television music program Countdown and a prominent promoter of Australian music, has died at age 83. According to his longtime friend and manager Mark Klemens, Meldrum passed away peacefully in the early hours of Monday morning at a hospital in Melbourne, a detail reported by the Guardian.

The Australian music journalist, broadcaster and producer was widely celebrated for helping expose Australian artists to international audiences and for bringing global music to Australia. Tributes have poured in from figures such as Human Nature and Jason Donovan, underscoring his lasting impact on the industry.
summary: Molly Meldrum, an Australian music journalist, broadcaster and producer known for hosting Countdown, died at age 83. He died peacefully in the early hours of Monday morning at a Melbourne hospital, according to his friend and manager Mark Klemens.

title: Zanbix 2 in 1 Galaxy Projector Night Light Review: Best Portable Star Projector
content:
The Zanbix 2 in 1 Galaxy Projector Night Light has emerged as a recommended option for consumers seeking a high-quality version of the viral gooseneck star projector. The device is powered via USB and features a flexible stalk, a slide slot, and a focus wheel mounted on the nose. While the projector bears a resemblance to standard models found on social media platforms like TikTok, YouTube, and Facebook, the reviewer notes that its larger lens provides significantly richer and clearer images than typical run-of-the-mill versions.

The product includes 13 swappable slides packed in a compact box. Of these, 10 feature astronomy-related images, including a black hole, the Magellanic Cloud, the Milky Way, and the Pillars of Creation. The remaining slides depict an angel and stars, a jellyfish, Santa, a T. Rex, and a whale and stars, with some images presented in black and white. The reviewer highlights that while some slides are artistic illustrations, others, such as the Pillars of Creation, are actual astronomical images. The static nature of the projections is a key distinction, as the device does not produce animated displays, contrary to some AI-generated advertisements that claim it can cast moving images like space whales.

In terms of functionality, the projector includes a four-hour shut-off timer for the projection mode and a 12-hour timer for the night light function. The flexible neck allows for easy adjustment, though the reviewer noted that some USB ports may have a tighter grip on the device. The projector can be powered by various USB sources, including laptops, desktops, chargers, and power banks, making it portable for use in different locations. The reviewer successfully tested the device using a TV’s USB socket and a power bank, emphasizing its convenience for on-the-go use.

The device is designed to be user-friendly, with no remote control or sound options required. The light portion warms up but does not get hot, making it safe for children to handle. The reviewer suggests that the projector is suitable for entertainment, relaxation, and education, potentially sparking interest in STEM subjects. While the selection of slides is considered ample, the lack of extra slide packs is noted as a minor disappointment. The projector is positioned as a pocket-friendly option that offers good value for money and portability, distinguishing it from larger, more complex models that may offer laser-dot stars or other features.
summary: It was only a matter of time, but AI has come for astronomy accessories. I’ve yet to see a fictional elderly craftsman begging you to buy his hand-carved telescopes; however, it has absolutely muddied the waters around this viral gooseneck Galaxy Projector Night Light.

title: SpaceX launches classified NROL-136 spy satellites from California
content:
SpaceX carried out a classified launch of the National Reconnaissance Office’s (NRO) NROL‑136 mission from Vandenberg Space Force Base on the California coast on November 22, 2026. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Launch Complex‑4E at 7:23 a.m. Eastern Time (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local). The launch marked the sixth NRO flight of the year, all of which have been executed with SpaceX’s Falcon 9.

Two minutes after liftoff, the first‑stage booster separated from the upper stage, which continued to carry the classified payloads into low‑Earth orbit. The booster then reversed course and landed at Landing Zone 4 about seven and a half minutes after launch. This was the 14th flight for booster B1097, which had previously launched NASA’s Sentinel‑6B, NROL‑172, USSF‑259 for the U.S. Space Force, and eight Starlink missions.

NROL‑136 is the 15th mission dedicated to building the NRO’s “proliferated architecture,” a network of satellites developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The constellation, begun in May 2024 with NROL‑146, is intended to increase coverage and improve the capability and resilience of U.S. intelligence operations in space. The agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL‑136 or details about their onboard technologies.
summary: SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California.

title: Florida prisoners testify that concrete prison heat reached 119°F heat index
content: Temperatures in a concrete facility contributed to one man’s death after he struggled to breathe, prisoners allege On Tuesday afternoon Dwayne Wilson, 69, a thin Black man dressed in a light gray prison uniform, testified about the stifling heat he experienced in the Dade correctional institute, a concrete state prison south of Miami, Florida, without air conditioning. He removed his glasses and wiped his eyes as he spoke. “It was so hot,” he said, his voice catching. “It’s so hot sometimes you have to put water on the floor just to try to keep cool.” Wilson said he’s housed in the H dorms, a T-shaped building with one-to-two-person cells, nicknamed “hell dorm” by prisoners because its concrete walls radiate heat absorbed from the sun. The plaintiff’s law firm, the Florida Justice Institute, convinced a judge to allow 31 sensors to be temporarily installed throughout the prison during the summer of 2025. They recorded temperature and humidity levels that Stefano Shiavon, a professor of civil and environmental engineering with expertise in thermal comfort, used to calculate the heat index. He found it to be above 88F (31C) 97% of the time, with the highest heat indexes often recorded at night, including one reading in the H dorm dayroom equivalent to 119F (48C) at 10pm one July day last year. “The walls sweat,” Wilson said. “It’s miserable in the cell at night because, again, it’s so hot. No air comes to the bed we sleep at and the bed is soaked in sweat.”
summary: Florida prisoners testify that concrete prison heat reached 119°F heat index.

content:
Lipodystrophy is a serious metabolic disease defined by abnormal lipid storage, where ingested fats bypass adipose tissue and deposit in the liver, muscle, or heart. This redistribution leads to significant metabolic consequences, including fatty liver and type 2 diabetes, while the visible fat changes and associated symptoms cause considerable distress for patients.

The underlying causes of the condition may stem from a congenital gene mutation, an immune disorder, or an infection.
summary: Scientists have identified a new transport pathway that explains how caveolin‑1 helps cells store fat. In lipodystrophy, ingested fats are not stored in adipose tissue but accumulate in the liver, muscle, or heart, leading to fatty liver and type 2 diabetes.

summary: The author covered themselves in various sleep‑tracking devices—including smartwatches, smart rings, smart bands, sleep earbuds and sleep masks—to evaluate their monitoring capabilities. title: NASA launches Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for US military
content:
On November 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on the classified STS‑33 mission for the U. S. Military.  The launch occurred at night, making it the third nighttime launch in the shuttle program and the thirty‑second overall mission.  Five astronauts were aboard, and their objective was to deploy a classified payload for the U. S. Department of Defense.

The payload carried on STS‑33 is believed to have been a spy satellite of the Magnum type.  What the Magnum satellite was intended to do in orbit remains classified.  NASA and the military had carried out several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites, reflecting the dual civilian and military roles envisioned for the Space Transportation System.

The shuttle program was designed as a compromise between civilian science and commercial objectives and the Department of Defense’s need to deploy and retrieve reconnaissance satellites.  After the Challenger disaster, it was decided that the shuttle would be used by the military only when it was essential to national security, with other missions handled by expendable launch vehicles.

During the STS‑33 flight, the crew also celebrated Thanksgiving in space.  The holiday began with a toilet malfunction that the astronauts spent most of the day repairing before enjoying their turkey together.

The story is part of the On This Day In Space archive, which documents key moments in spaceflight history.
summary: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.

content: Research indicates that a parasite can increase mice’s attractiveness to blood‑feeding triatomine bugs, a change that may help the parasite spread. The report notes that parasites such as Trypanosoma rangeli and Trypanosoma cruzi move between mammals and triatomine bugs, with bugs picking up the organisms from infected mammals and mammals becoming infected after contact with infected bugs.
summary: Trypanosoma rangeli and Trypanosoma cruzi can be transmitted between mammals and triatomine bugs. Bugs acquire the parasites by feeding on infected mammals, and mammals can become infected after contact with infected bugs.
author: Phys.org

title: Milky Way simulation reaches record resolution using three supercomputers
content:
A team of researchers, including scientists from the University of Tokyo, has created a new method for modeling the Milky Way that reaches a level of detail never before achieved. By harnessing the combined power of three of the world’s most powerful supercomputers, the team simulated the entire galaxy down to the scale of individual stars.

The simulation employed an AI‑accelerated model designed to operate across multiple hardware platforms. According to the researchers, this approach can enhance scientific insight into how galaxies evolve.
summary: Researchers including those from the University of Tokyo developed a new method to model the Milky Way at unprecedented detail, simulating the entire galaxy down to individual stars. They used three of the world’s most powerful supercomputers with an AI‑accelerated model that runs on multiple hardware platforms, which can improve understanding of galactic evolution.
author: Phys.org

title: Prospect union says it has lost confidence in UKRI chief Ian Chapman over planned cuts
content:
Prospect, a trade union representing scientists and engineers, has written to UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) that it has lost confidence in the agency’s chief executive. The union cites concerns about plans for major cuts to science and research funding.

The letter, from Mike Clancy, general secretary of Prospect, to Ian Chapman, chief executive of UKRI, is the latest development in a row over changes in funding for projects and research facilities.
summary: Prospect general secretary Mike Clancy wrote to UKRI chief executive Ian Chapman saying the union has lost confidence in his leadership. The union cited concerns about plans for major cuts to funding for projects and research facilities.
author: Guardian Science

title: Super El Niño this year expected to worsen global hunger
content: The Super El Niño this year is expected to produce wetter weather in some areas and severe drought in others. Coupled with ongoing wars and reductions in foreign aid, the phenomenon could cause millions of people in vulnerable nations to face food shortages.
summary: The Super El Niño this year is bringing wetter conditions to some regions and massive drought to others. Together with ongoing wars and cuts to foreign aid, the weather event could leave millions of people in vulnerable countries without enough to eat.
author: Wired

title: Vibe-coding revolution expands to all gadgets
content:
The Stepback is a weekly newsletter that distills a single key story from the tech world. It arrives in subscribers’ inboxes every Sunday at 8 AM ET, and readers can opt in through a link provided in the announcement. For deeper coverage of “vibe‑hacking” across devices, the newsletter points to David Pierce.

The current issue highlights a “vibe‑coding revolution” that is set to reach all gadgets. According to the piece, the trend is not a brand‑new capability introduced by large language models; rather, it builds on a long history of users hacking, modding, jailbreaking, and tweaking hardware.

What is new, the article notes, is the ease with which people worldwide can now use large language models to hack their hardware. This accessibility marks a shift in how consumers approach device customization and modification.
summary: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on the vibe-hacking of everything, follow David Pierce.
author: The Verge

title: Apple HomeView’s Audio Review: Decent for Size, Not a Replacement for Larger Speakers
content:
Apple’s HomeView, Apple’s first smart display, has been praised for its role as a music controller and for delivering decent sound given its compact size. After publishing an initial review, many readers asked how the device performs as a smart speaker, prompting the author to conduct additional audio tests and evaluate support for third‑party music apps. The follow‑up article addresses those questions, noting a few frustrations encountered during testing.

The author compares the HomeView’s audio to other popular speakers, including the HomePod Mini, Sonos One, and the full‑size HomePod. The conclusion is that the HomeView is not intended to replace larger or similarly sized speakers; those options provide noticeably better sound quality. In terms of size and audio performance, the HomeView is close to the Sonos One and HomePod Mini but still falls short of their capabilities.
summary: Apple HomeView is a great music controller and a decent speaker for its size. It is not a replacement for larger speakers such as the Sonos One or full-size HomePod.
author: The Verge

title: Tamagotchi digital pet craze marks 30th anniversary
content:
The new episode of Version History explores the rise of the Tamagotchi, the tiny digital pets that captured the imaginations of millions of kids in the late 1990s. The show examines how the devices, which required constant feeding, cleaning, and attention, became an overnight sensation and how parents were suddenly faced with new responsibilities when their children went to school.

The series celebrates the 30th anniversary of the Tamagotchi’s launch, noting that the craze lasted only a few years despite its massive cultural impact. In the episode, host David Pierce is joined by The Verge’s Mia to dig deep into the story behind the phenomenon.
summary: The tiny Tamagotchi digital pets became an overnight sensation among late‑1990s kids, with millions signing up to care for the crying, hungry, constantly dirty creatures. The story celebrates its 30th anniversary this week even though the craze lasted only a few years.
author: The Verge

title: Love Me one-man show uses Auracast headphones at SoHo Playhouse
content:
A performance of Love Me is being staged at the SoHo Playhouse, a 178‑seat venue housed in a 200‑year‑old row house in New York City. Audience members are given a black drawstring bag containing wired headphones that connect to a small Auracast receiver, and they are asked to put the headphones on shortly after the show begins.

The production uses Auracast broadcasts both to enhance accessibility and to shape its sound design, making the headphones an essential element of the storytelling. Love Me is a one‑man show created by stand‑up comedian and former Saturday Night Live writer Drew Michael together with director Prashanth Venkataramanujam. The piece explores themes of love and the desire for connection across five chapters.
summary: Love Me uses Auracast broadcasts both for accessibility and the sound design. | Photo: Curtis Brown Up a few concrete steps and through the front door of a 200-year-old row house in New York City, I follow a crowd of people into the 178-seat SoHo Playhouse.
author: The Verge

title: Nintendo Switch 2 Bundles $50 Off for Black Friday
content:
Nintendo has announced a Black Friday promotion that lets buyers save $50 on one of its two current Switch 2 bundles. The discount begins today, November 22, and runs through Saturday, December 5, giving shoppers time to decide after Cyber Monday. The offer temporarily rolls back the $50 price increase that took effect in early September.

The Mario Kart World bundle is now $499.99, down from $549.99. It includes the Switch 2 console, a digital copy of Mario Kart World, and three months of Nintendo Switch Online. The Nintendo Switch Sports Resort bundle remains at $529.99 and contains the Switch Sports Resort title. Both bundles are available from Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Nintendo’s own storefront.

Nintendo’s Switch 2, released in mid‑2025, can play nearly all original Switch games and is wirelessly compatible with the older system’s Joy‑Con and Switch Pro controllers. Recent releases such as the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time add to the library of titles that may motivate a purchase.

For those planning to add a Switch 2 to their collection, guides are available that recommend accessories such as tempered glass screen protectors, protective cases, and additional controllers to enhance protection and enjoyment.
summary: Nintendo Switch 2 Bundles $50 Off for Black Friday.
author: The Verge

title: GLP-1 weight‑loss drugs could free up 32 million hectares of farmland, study finds
content:
GLP‑1 weight‑loss medicines, including Ozempic and Wegovy, may influence more than just individual waistlines. A new study suggests that if these appetite‑suppressing drugs were widely adopted, they could reshape the global food system by reducing overall calorie demand. Lower demand would prompt producers to adjust output, which could shift production patterns, alter prices, change trade flows, and reduce the amount of land needed for agriculture.

The researchers employed a sophisticated computer simulation to model a range of scenarios, from concentrated use in high‑income countries to broad global access. Their analysis focused on adults living with obesity, the primary target group for GLP‑1 therapies.

According to the simulation, widespread use of GLP‑1 medicines could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050. Additionally, the study estimates that the resulting decrease in calorie consumption could free up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than the country of Italy—for alternative uses.
summary: GLP-1 weight‑loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could impact the global food system by reducing calorie intake. Researchers estimate that widespread use among adults with obesity could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050 and free up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land.
author: Ars Technica

title: Best gifts for every generation chosen by people aged 2 to 103
content:
A recent Guardian survey asked people of every age—from Gen Alpha preschoolers to retired boomers, celebrities and Guardian writers—what they would like for Christmas 2026. Respondents were prompted with the question, “How old are you, and what would you like for Christmas?” The aim was to capture the gift preferences of a wide range of generations.

The findings are intended to help shoppers tailor their presents across age groups and may offer insight into the tastes of each cohort. The survey notes that some answers could be surprising, reflecting the diverse interests that span the generational spectrum.

Among the responses, a 67‑year‑old boomer listed a Nintendo Switch, while 30‑somethings mentioned collecting vinyl records and brewing craft beer as their desired gifts.
summary: The Guardian surveyed hundreds of individuals from preschoolers to retired boomers, celebrities and writers about their Christmas wish lists for 2026. Their answers, including a boomer wanting a Nintendo Switch and 30‑somethings collecting vinyl and brewing craft beer, show varied gift preferences across generations.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Howard Lutnick faces scrutiny over Nvidia scandal and China chip sales
content:
Howard Lutnick, billionaire commerce secretary and close ally of Donald Trump, faces scrutiny after a sex scandal reveals his role in sales of chips to China.  

As Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January, Lutnick is emerging as their prime target. He is resisting calls to resign amid bipartisan outcry over his involvement in a scandal at AI company Nvidia and the sale of microchips to China, the US’s principal geopolitical rival in the race for AI supremacy.
summary: Billionaire commerce secretary Howard Lutnick is under scrutiny after a sex scandal revealed his involvement in Nvidia and the sale of microchips to China. He is resisting calls to resign amid bipartisan outcry as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Trump says FBI hack “not good” but could have benefits
content: Former President Donald Trump said the reported FBI hack was “not good” but could have benefits. The breach occurred amid a wave of U.S. tech outages that have disrupted travel, communications, banking, and an internal system used by the National Security Agency.
summary: The reported breach comes amid a wave of tech outages in the US, which have impacted travel, communications and banking, as well as an internal system used by the National Security Agency.
author: Euronews

title: Thousands march in Lisbon under rain demanding higher wages and better pensions
content: Thousands marched through Lisbon on Saturday, 21 November 2026, braving heavy rain to call for higher wages, better pensions and measures to curb the rising cost of living. The protest occurred just days before Portugal’s parliamentary budget vote.
summary: Thousands of people marched through Lisbon on Saturday 21 November 2026, braving heavy rain to demand higher wages, better pensions and measures to tackle the rising cost of living. The demonstration took place just days before Portugal's parliamentary budget vote.
author: Euronews

title: Tracking site says alleged Iranian tanker in Strait of Hormuz does not exist
content: A tracking website reported that a claimed Iranian tanker said to be sailing through the Strait of Hormuz does not exist. The U.S. military noted that Saturday marked the 130th consecutive day of its naval blockade of Iran, which it says is stopping the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps from exporting “billions of dollars in crude oil.”
summary: A tracking site reported that the Iranian tanker said to be sailing through the Strait of Hormuz does not exist. The US military said Saturday marked 130 consecutive days of its naval blockade against Iran, which it says is preventing the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps from exporting "billions of dollars in crude oil."
author: Euronews

title: Over 200 mascots gather in Saitama, Japan, for fan-filled parade
content: More than 200 colourful mascots gathered in Saitama, Japan, where they entertained tens of thousands of fans with dancing, parades and photo opportunities. The event featured Kumamon, the well‑known black bear mascot, among the many characters on display.
summary: More than 200 colourful mascots gathered in Saitama, Japan, delighting tens of thousands of fans with dancing, parades and photo opportunities. Kumamon, the country's famous black bear mascot, was among the stars.
author: Euronews

title: Russian strike in Dymer near Kyiv leaves up to seven feared trapped under rubble
content: A Russian strike on Sunday partially destroyed an apartment building in Dymer, a town north of Kyiv. Nine residents, one of them a child, were evacuated, while rescuers continued to search the debris for as many as seven additional people believed to be trapped beneath the rubble.
summary: A Russian strike partially destroyed an apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv, on Sunday. Rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child, and are searching the rubble for up to seven others feared trapped.
author: Euronews

title: Mongolia prepares snap presidential election after President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa resigns
content: Mongolia is preparing for its first early presidential election after President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa resigned amid corruption allegations. Prior to leaving office, the outgoing president called for constitutional reform. The snap vote will determine his successor.
summary: Mongolia is preparing for its first early presidential election. President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa resigned amid corruption allegations and had called for constitutional reform before leaving office.
author: Euronews

title: Indonesian factory fire: emergency crews retrieve at least six body bags
content: Emergency workers recovered at least six body bags following a factory fire in Indonesia. Video footage shared on social media by the National Search and Rescue Agency (Basarnas) showed the crews examining the charred remains of the building.
summary: Emergency workers recovered at least six body bags after a factory fire in Indonesia. Video posted by Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency (Basarnas) showed emergency crews looking through the charred remains of the building.
author: Euronews

title: Europe sees third day of protests over cost of living and housing
content: Sunday marked the third straight day of protests across Europe, following large demonstrations on Friday and smaller rallies on Saturday in countries ranging from Portugal to France. Demonstrators have centered their actions on the rising cost of living and the need for affordable housing. In France, the protests have now occurred for six consecutive weekends, reports Ophelie Jacobson.
summary: Sunday marked the third consecutive day of protests across Europe, following large demonstrations on Friday and smaller rallies on Saturday from Portugal to France. The protests have centered on the rising cost of living and access to affordable housing, with France seeing demonstrations for six weekends in a row.
author: France 24

title: South Korea education minister resigns after AI cheating scandal in tax exam
content: South Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday after a major cheating scandal emerged ahead of the nation’s university entrance exams. The scandal involved the top scorer on a national tax accountant exam, who admitted using a miniature camera and a smartphone to obtain a near‑perfect result, according to Jack Pownall.
summary: South Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday after a cheating scandal erupted ahead of the university entrance exams. The scandal involved the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam who admitted using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near‑perfect result.
author: France 24

title: Princess Catherine stars in “Heal” documentary about cancer and 24‑hour mountain trek
content: A new documentary called Heal follows Britain’s Princess Catherine as she navigates life after a cancer diagnosis in 2024. The film tracks the 44‑year‑old attempting to summit the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours, and the trailer shows her reflecting on healing as a journey. Ophelie Jacobson reports.
summary: A new documentary called Heal follows Britain’s Princess Catherine as she lives with a cancer diagnosis made in 2024. The film shows the 44‑year‑old attempting to summit the highest peaks in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours while reflecting on healing.
author: France 24

title: Former Italian national police chief found dead amid bombing cover‑up probe
content: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said she was shocked after the body of a former national police chief was discovered on Saturday. The deceased had been under investigation for an alleged cover‑up in an inquiry into a bombing tied to organised crime in Sicily, according to reporter Jennie Shin.
summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said she was shocked after a former national police chief was found dead on Saturday. He had been under investigation for an alleged cover‑up in a Sicily organised‑crime bombing inquiry.
author: France 24

title: Fire at Indonesian sweets factory kills three, leaves 36 missing
content: A fire erupted at an Indonesian factory that produces sweets and snack products, killing at least three people and leaving dozens missing. Fifteen individuals were rescued alive from the plant, while firefighters continued to combat flames in several sections of the facility more than 12 hours after the blaze began. The cause of the fire has not been determined; survivors reported that it started in a cooling unit on the third floor.
summary: At least three people were killed and 36 are missing after a fire broke out at an Indonesian factory that produces sweets and snack products. Fifteen people were rescued alive while firefighters continued battling flames more than 12 hours after the blaze began, which survivors said started in a cooling unit on the third floor.
author: France 24

title: Israel opens investigation into West Bank fires targeting Palestinian vehicles
content:
Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were vandalised and set on fire in four villages in the occupied West Bank. Local activists say the attacks were carried out by Israeli settlers. Reports indicate that around eight vehicles were torched and racist slogans were sprayed on walls, prompting Israeli soldiers and police to deploy to the area.

The incidents come amid a surge in settler violence that began with the outbreak of the Gaza war in October 2023. According to an AFP tally, more than 1,100 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli soldiers or settlers in the West Bank since that time. The attacks also follow recent sanctions announced by the UK and Australia against eight Israeli companies involved in settlement activity.

France 24 correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky shares further details from Jerusalem.
summary: Israeli authorities opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were vandalised and set on fire in four West Bank villages, allegedly by Israeli settlers. Israeli soldiers and police were deployed to the area after eight vehicles were torched and racist slogans sprayed on walls.
author: France 24

title: Anthropic's Levent Alpöge Publishes 17-Million Line AI Proof of Riemann Hypothesis
content:
An AI system announced a new mathematical claim on Friday, with Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge publishing what he describes as a proof of the Riemann hypothesis—a Millennium Prize Problem—encoded in 17 million lines of code that no human has read in its entirety.  

Physicist Tony Padilla told Tech 24 that confirming the proof could take years and suggested that Alpöge should explain the method by which the result was obtained.
summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge released a 17‑million‑line code claiming to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a Millennium Prize Problem. Physicist Tony Padilla said verification could take years and urged Alpöge to share how he arrived at the proof.
author: France 24

title: Xi hosts Trump and Putin at Shenzhen summit; COP31 in Turkey and French protests rise
content: The week’s headline moments were captured in striking images: in Shenzhen, President Xi Jinping hosted former U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin for an unprecedented summit, while in Antalya, Turkey, delegates engaged in tough talks at COP31. Meanwhile, France saw another week of protests over the cost of living. FRANCE 24 reviewed these pivotal scenes.
summary: President Xi Jinping hosted US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at an unprecedented Shenzhen summit in China. COP31 held tough talks in Antalya, Turkey, and French protests over the cost of living continued.
author: France 24

title: China and ASEAN deadlock stalls South China Sea code of conduct slated for 2026
content: The Philippines has expressed a desire for a South China Sea code of conduct to be finalized by 2026. However, ongoing disagreements between China and ASEAN member states are hindering progress toward reaching such an agreement.
summary: The Philippines sought to have a South China Sea code of conduct in place by 2026. Ongoing disagreements between China and ASEAN countries are delaying the agreement.
author: DW World

title: Indian Youth Congress warns of more Meta protests after Hyderabad police clash
content:
Members of the Congress party clashed with police outside Meta’s local offices in Hyderabad on Friday. Protesters carried placards, chanted slogans, stormed into the building that houses Meta’s offices, smashed plants to the ground, and confronted police, as shown in footage released by the Indian Youth Congress’s X account.

The youth wing of India’s main opposition party warned that more protests would follow, citing Meta’s removal of some of its members’ accounts. The warning came a day after the police clash at the tech firm’s offices.
summary: The Indian Youth Congress cautioned of further protests over Meta’s removal of some members’ accounts after its members clashed with police outside Meta’s Hyderabad office on Friday. Protesters stormed the building, smashed plants, carried placards, chanted slogans and confronted police, footage posted on the Youth Congress’s X account.
author: Guardian World

title: British swimmer Lewis Pugh completes three‑day, 9.3‑mile swim of Strait of Hormuz
content:
Lewis Pugh, a British endurance swimmer and UN patron of the oceans, completed a three‑day swim through the Strait of Hormuz to draw attention to the environmental cost of the Iran war. During the crossing he witnessed ships ablaze and fighter jets overhead as the conflict continues.

Pugh swam the 9.3‑mile (15 km) length of the waterway, a key route for oil shipments from the Middle East. His swim aimed to highlight the potential ecological damage that could result from ongoing hostilities in the region.
summary: British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh, a UN patron of the oceans, completed a three‑day swim of the 9.3‑mile (15 km) Strait of Hormuz. He did so to highlight the environmental cost of the Iran war, observing ships ablaze and fighter jets overhead.
author: Guardian World

title: UK and EU finalize SPS food deal to end most Brexit checks, welcomed by British firms
content:
British producers have broadly welcomed the United Kingdom’s new sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) deal with the European Union, which is designed to eliminate most physical checks on food, plants and animal products. Exporters said the agreement signals an end to costly Brexit‑related inspections, though they expressed frustration that full implementation will take a long time.

The SPS deal is expected to benefit Britain’s food exporters and allow UK delicatessens and other small retailers to resume importing European cheese and wine, products that had become economically unviable under the previous check regime.
summary: UK and EU finalize SPS food deal to end most Brexit checks, welcomed by British firms.
author: Guardian World

title: EU, UK and developing nations reject Cop31 deal that omitted fossil fuels
content: EU, UK and some of developing world object to main text that ‘failed to meet the moment’ and did not mention fossil fuels • Cop31 live blog: longest climate summit ever faces collapse The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world rejected what they called an unacceptable deal on the future of the climate, which failed even to mention fossil fuels, in a dramatic finish to the Cop31 UN talks in Turkey. The proposed deal “failed to meet the moment”, said Ireland’s environment minister, Darragh O’Brien, speaking for the EU. “We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required. [It] does not even mention fossil fuels.”
summary: The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world rejected the proposed deal at the Cop31 UN talks in Turkey. Ireland’s environment minister Darragh O’Brien said the text failed to meet the moment and did not even mention fossil fuels.
author: Guardian World

title: Australia urged to cut imported fossil fuels as global supply shocks loom
content:
A new report from the Grattan Institute urges the Australian government to lessen the nation’s dependence on imported fossil fuels. The think‑tank warns that heavy reliance on overseas fuel leaves the country vulnerable to global supply shocks, citing the war in Iran as an example.

The report recommends capping diesel tax credits that currently benefit mining and primary‑industry firms, while directing incentives toward electric trucks and expanding the electric‑vehicle charging network. It also proposes subsidies for electric vehicles aimed at lower‑income households and the construction of “clean” refineries to replace imported fuel.

According to Grattan, implementing these measures could reduce Australians’ fuel costs by thousands of dollars each year. The institute’s recommendations have already attracted criticism from business groups.
summary: Australia urged to cut imported fossil fuels as global supply shocks loom.
author: Guardian World

title: Australian parliament sets swearing record as MPs Jacqui Lambie and Garth Hamilton curse
content: One serial sweary offender, Jacqui Lambie, says it wouldn’t be an Australian parliament ‘without a few swear words thrown in’ Want to get more charts in your inbox every fortnight? Sign up for The Crunch here When Liberal MP Garth Hamilton stormed out of parliament in June, slamming his hands on his desk and calling out “fucking bullshit” the speaker of the house, Milton Dick, called it “a new low” in federal politics. Dick may have been on to something.
summary: Australian parliament sets swearing record as MPs Jacqui Lambie and Garth Hamilton curse.
author: Guardian World

title: Fire at West Jakarta confectionery factory kills three, leaves 36 missing
content:
A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta has killed three people and left 36 others missing, according to an Indonesian rescue official. Drone footage captured large sections of the plant destroyed, with portions of the roof collapsed and smoke still rising from the complex.

Relatives of the missing victims gathered at the factory’s entrance seeking updates. Rescuers shared photos and videos showing officers entering the charred building on Sunday, searching for those still unaccounted for while small fires continued to burn in some areas.
summary: A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta killed three people and left 36 missing, according to an Indonesian rescue official. Rescuers entered the charred building, where the roof had collapsed, smoke rose and small fires continued burning.
author: Guardian World

title: Bank of England directors profited from post‑abolition Cuban copper slave labor
content:
New research shows that the British‑led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester by supplying copper deposits while enslaving African people.  

The study also finds that British businesses run by long‑serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire.  

Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, historian Chris Evans has documented.
summary: Bank of England directors profited from post‑abolition Cuban copper slave labor.
author: Guardian World

title: Danny Kelly, 69, dies; celebrated football broadcaster remembered for passionate radio
content:
Danny Kelly, the journalist and broadcaster who died last week at the age of 69, is remembered for his enduring impact on sports radio. The article highlights a specific moment from 29 October 2008, during the injury time of a 4-3 Arsenal victory over Tottenham at the Emirates. As Aaron Lennon scored the winning goal, Kelly, broadcasting from the TalkSport studio at 18 Hatfields in London, reacted with a loud, guttural noise before exclaiming, “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.”

The piece describes this broadcast as a brilliant example of radio commentary, featuring Kelly alongside reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore. The source notes that while the on-pitch scene was chaotic, the real entertainment was occurring in the studio. Kelly’s passionate reaction to the goal, which involved Lennon being enveloped by teammates and pitch invaders, is cited as evidence of his status as one of the greats of the medium, even as the broadcasting landscape continued to change rapidly.
summary: Danny Kelly, a journalist and broadcaster, died last week at age 69. He was celebrated for his passionate football commentary on radio, famously exclaiming "I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT" during a live match.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Elliot Anderson halts Manchester City’s losing run but boos greet Fulham draw
content:
Manchester City entered the match against Fulham in a slump, having gone four games without a win and three games without a victory. The Premier League side managed a 0‑0 draw that ended the losing streak, but the result was met with boos from home supporters. City’s form has deteriorated while the club awaits the outcome of a disciplinary review that found it guilty of financial breaches.

The draw featured a disallowed goal by Erling Haaland, a goal from Rodrigo Muniz that capitalised on City’s porous defence, and a contribution from Elliot Anderson that was crucial in securing the point. Despite the defensive lapses, the club was not seen as deserving any further criticism.
summary: Manchester City are living in Premier League purgatory, without a win in four, but at least against Fulham they ended a three-game losing run. As they await their fate after being found guilty of financial breaches, their form has slumped.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Hearts crush 10-man Dundee 8-0 in Scottish Premiership
content:
Dundee suffered an 8‑0 defeat to Hearts, the biggest loss of the season for the side. Hearts’ manager Wouter Vrancken called the win “remarkable” and said it was the club’s best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle. The result ended Dundee’s run of three consecutive defeats.

The scorers for Hearts were Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kaboré, who each netted twice, with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and an own goal by Ryan Finnigan adding to the tally.

In other Scottish Premiership fixtures, Celtic beat St Mirren 4‑1 and Rangers defeated Motherwell 2‑1. Dundee manager Steven Pressley admitted he was “embarrassed … I apologise” for the loss.
summary: Hearts defeated Dundee 8-0 after Dundee were reduced to ten men, with Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kaboré each scoring twice. Manager Wouter Vrancken said it was the team's best performance since he took charge and that it ended a run of three defeats.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Coventry beat Crystal Palace to keep Palace bottom as Thomas Frank's debut ends in loss
content:
Coventry secured a narrow victory over Crystal Palace, a result that left the visitors at the bottom of the league after five consecutive defeats. The match featured a new manager for Palace, Thomas Frank, who introduced a new formation but could not prevent the defensive lapses that plagued both sides in a chaotic first half.

Palace managed to equalise twice and appeared to stabilise after the break, yet a triple substitution made by Frank Lampard with around 20 minutes remaining swung momentum back to Coventry. In the final five minutes, a long throw was met by Brandon Thomas‑Asante, whose header was deflected by goalkeeper Dean Henderson, then struck Dwight McNeil before finding the net.

Lampard praised his side’s spirit, noting the impact of the substitutes and describing it as a positive sign for the squad. The win kept Crystal Palace at the foot of the table and marked a disappointing start for Thomas Frank.
summary: New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Midshipmen’s stadium letters switched from “GO NAVY” to “GO ARMY” in overnight prank
content: Cadets rearranged bolted-down seats overnight Navy workers spent four hours undoing stunt Rival academies have long history of pranks The large letters that spell “GO NAVY” in the upper seating level of the Naval Academy’s football stadium were changed to “GO ARMY” in an elaborate overnight prank before the Midshipmen hosted No 24 Memphis on Saturday. The stunt involved rearranging the blue and yellow seat backs at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium in Annapolis, Maryland, a task made considerably more complicated by the fact that the seats are bolted into place.
summary: Cadets rearranged the blue and yellow seat backs at Navy‑Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, changing the “GO NAVY” letters to “GO ARMY” before the Midshipmen hosted No 24 Memphis on Saturday. Navy workers spent four hours undoing the stunt, which involved moving bolted‑down seats and continues a long history of rival academy pranks.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Grey Dawning wins Betfair Chase at Haydock as Lossiemouth gives Mullins third Punchestown win
content: Grey Dawning, the 11‑10 favourite, won at Haydock, becoming a dual winner of the Betfair Chase.
